title: Applicant Experience with Virtual Interviews in Neurology Residency Recruitment: A Longitudinal Survey
content: Background: Travel restrictions during the COVID-19 pandemic disrupted medical education and residency recruitment. National organizations including ACGME and AAN recommended virtual interviews for adult and pediatric residency programs. This study provides insights from a single-center survey of applicants’ experiences with virtual interview process over three years. Methods: An online, anonymous survey was sent to 300 applicants who interviewed at our adult neurology residency program during the 2020-2021 (Year 1), 2021-2022 (Year 2), and 2023-2024 (Year 3) cycles. The survey was emailed after Rank Order List Submission, and responses were collected over 60 days. Results: Preference for virtual interviews increased from 29% in Year 1 to 41% in Year 3. Key factors influencing the rank list were interactions with the Program Director (65-80% of the applicants) and Program Coordinator, as well as program reputation and faculty interviews. A total of 110 applicants responded across the three cycles. The majority were non-US IMGs (59% Year 1, 61.3% Year 2, 47% Year 3). Most applicants applied to over 60 programs, with 77% doing so in Year 2. Over time, the number of interviews accepted declined, shifting from 10–20 in Year 1 to fewer than 10 in Year 3. Program websites were the most valuable resource, cited by 72–76% of applicants, followed by program-run webinars, open houses, and social media. Among social media platforms, X (formerly Twitter) was used more frequently than Facebook or Reddit. Over 80% of applicants reported no time zone issues, and Zoom was the preferred platform. Connectivity issues decreased over the years. Conclusions: This study provides valuable insights into applicants’ experiences and perceptions of the virtual interview process. While it does increase equity and access, it also leads to a greater trend of applying to more programs than usual. Interactions with Program Directors and Coordinators are instrumental in influencing applicants’ ranking decisions. More studies can help guide the future direction of this process.
